findings.body:
This generated bundle adds `a.run=function(s){return eval(s)}` while `src/app.ts` is unchanged and only defines `init()`. That is not a toolchain rebuild: it is new behavior, and `eval(s)` executes arbitrary attacker-controlled strings in the page context if anything passes user or remote input into `run`.

Regenerate dist from source, or land the real source change (without `eval`) in the same PR before shipping the bundle.

Only `dist/app.min.js` is in the commit; there is no `src/` change and no build-config change. A claimed post-upgrade regeneration should either be a byte-equivalent re-emit of existing source or land alongside the source that produced it. As landed, source and dist have diverged and reviewers cannot audit the new API in TypeScript.

summary:
## Verdict

Do not merge: the only change is a hand-edited generated bundle that introduces an `eval`-based API with no matching source change.

## What changed

This PR touches a single omitted/generated file, `dist/app.min.js` (+1/−1). `src/app.ts` is identical at base and head and still only exports `init()`. The PR description frames this as a toolchain rebuild; a pure rebuild would not add new runtime surface that is absent from source.

## Why this blocks

The new bundle body wires `app.run = function (s) { return eval(s) }`. Any caller that can influence `s` gets arbitrary JavaScript execution in the page context. That is a production security defect, and it cannot be a faithful emit of the current TypeScript entrypoint.

## What to do

1. Restore `dist/app.min.js` from the last known good build, or regenerate it from `src/` with the normal build pipeline and commit that output only if it matches source.
2. If `run()` / dynamic evaluation is intentional, land it in `src/app.ts` first with a non-`eval` implementation (or a tightly audited one), tests, and then rebuild dist in the same PR.
3. Treat a dist-only behavioral edit as a supply-chain/review bypass risk going forward: generated artifacts should not gain APIs the source tree does not define.

**Recommendation:** request-changes
